accepted.question_text: For cyclic codes in the classical families discussed in the chapter, what are the exact minimum distances of Bose–Chaudhuri–Hocquenghem (BCH) codes and quadratic residue (QR) codes in the cases where those distances are still unknown?
accepted.context_brief: Exact distances of BCH and QR codes

evidence.quote: The minimum dis￾tance of GRM codes is known (see comments of Section 3.2 and 3.4.1). This is generally not known for BCH codes and QR codes.

accepted.question_text: Find a decoding algorithm for quadratic residue codes, since the chapter states that no decoding algorithm was known for them.

evidence.quote: There is no decoding algorithm known for QR codes.

accepted.question_text: For primitive binary BCH codes of length 2^m−1, determine the exact minimum-distance behavior in the remaining unresolved case m = 12 discussed by the chapter.

evidence.quote: By using Newton identities they proved that two such codes have true minimum distance δ + 2. These are the BCH codes with designed distance 59 and 61. At the moment the case m = 12 remains open.

accepted.question_text: For the binary narrow-sense BCH codes of length 511, determine the true minimum distances of the six unresolved codes with designed distances 59, 61, 75, 77, 85, and 107.

evidence.quote: The value of d is not known for six codes. These are the BCH codes with designed distance 59 , 61 , 75 , 77 , 85 and 107.

accepted.question_text: Develop a satisfactory way to determine or sharply estimate the minimum distances of the duals of primitive BCH codes, since the chapter reports that this approximation problem remained open.

evidence.quote: Generally the numerical results obtained in this way show that the approximation of the minimum distance of the duals of primitive BCH codes remains an open problem.

accepted.question_text: Determine the weight enumerators of generalized Reed–Muller (GRM) codes in general, since the chapter states that these weight enumerators are not known.

evidence.quote: The weight enumerators of GRM codes are not known.

accepted.question_text: For binary Reed–Muller codes, determine the weight enumerators of R_2(ν,m) in the unresolved range 3 ≤ ν ≤ m−4.

evidence.quote: It is an old problem to find the weight enumerators of R2(ν, m), 3 ≤ ν ≤ m − 4.

accepted.question_text: Determine the weight enumerator of the self-dual binary Reed–Muller code R_2(4,9), which the chapter identifies as the remaining unknown Reed–Muller weight enumerator at length 512.

evidence.quote: Since the dual of R2(3, 9) is R2(5, 9), only the weight enumerator of R2(4, 9), the self-dual code, remains unknown.

accepted.question_text: Beyond the known Reed–Muller cases, for which cyclic codes is the entire code generated by its minimum-weight codewords?

evidence.quote: This leads to the general problem: for which other cyclic codes does this property hold ?

accepted.question_text: Can the Newton-identity method described in the chapter be generalized so as to recover the minimum-weight codewords of generalized Reed–Muller codes of arbitrary order, or at least yield a shorter proof than the classical arguments?

evidence.quote: We cannot say, at present, if our method which leads to the description of the set of minimum weight codewords of GRM codes of some orders (Theorem 3.18) can be generalized to GRM codes of any order.

accepted.question_text: Classify binary cyclic codes with exactly two zeros by minimum distance and determine their weight enumerators, since the chapter says this classification had not been achieved and the weight-enumerator problem remained very difficult.

evidence.quote: This section is concerned with the classification of the codes Cr,s by means of their minimum distance. Our aim is to recall that this classification is not yet achieved; furthermore the determination of the weight enumerators ap￾pears as a most difficult problem.

accepted.question_text: Characterize new binary cyclic codes with two zeros that are optimal, or at least have minimum distance five, beyond the special families already known to the chapter.

evidence.quote: To characterize new cyclic codes with two zeros which are optimal, even not optimal but with minimum distance five, remains a hard open problem.

accepted.question_text: Welsh conjecture: for binary cyclic codes C_{1,ℓ} of length 2^m−1 with ℓ = 2^t + 3 and m = 2t + 1, prove or disprove that these codes have minimum distance five and the same weight enumerator as the 2-error-correcting BCH code.

evidence.quote: We want to mention the oldest conjecture, the so-called conjecture of Welsh: the codes C1,`, of length 2^m − 1, with ` = 2^t + 3 and m = 2^t + 1 , have minimum distance five; furthermore they have the same weight enumer￾ator as the 2-error-correcting BCH code.

accepted.question_text: Give a complete description of primitive binary cyclic codes of minimum distance three; the chapter reports only partial classifications and says the full description remained open.
accepted.context_brief: Primitive binary cyclic codes with d=3

evidence.quote: However the whole description of cyclic codes of minimum distance three remains an open, and apparently, difficult problem.

accepted.question_text: Determine the weight enumerators of cyclic codes whose duals are contained in the Reed–Muller code of order two, especially the cyclic codes whose zeros have the form α^(2^i+2^k), including the cases that appear to share the 3-error-correcting BCH weight enumerator.

evidence.quote: We do not know the weight enumerator of any cyclic code whose zeros have the form α^(2^i+2^k); for instance such codes which have the same weight enumerator as the 3-error-correcting BCH code are not yet characterized (see [144]).

accepted.question_text: Recover the original structure of a Goppa code from a permuted generator matrix alone, a problem the chapter singles out because of its relevance to understanding and potentially attacking McEliece-type constructions.

evidence.quote: On the other hand there is a famous open problem which is to recover the original structure of any Goppa code when only a permuted generator matrix is given.

accepted.question_text: Determine the automorphism groups of Goppa codes, since the chapter states that these groups were not known in general.

evidence.quote: The automorphism groups of Goppa codes are not known.

accepted.question_text: Characterize which classical Goppa codes, extended or not, are cyclic.

evidence.quote: the problem of the characterization of classi￾cal Goppa codes (extended or not) which are cyclic remains open.

accepted.question_text: Determine the complete weight enumerator of the Melas code, since the chapter explicitly says that this remained open and ties it to Kloosterman sums.

evidence.quote: The problem of the complete determination of the weight enumerator of the Melas code remains open; any result on the number of words of a given weight could apply to the problem of the values of Kloosterman sums.

accepted.question_text: Are all families of cyclic codes asymptotically bad, or do there exist asymptotically good cyclic linear codes?

evidence.quote: Whether or not there exist good linear codes which are also cyclic remains an open problem.
